picks.title: Replay Buffers Beat Summaries for Long-Running Coding Agents

what.text: Swapped the summarised memory in a coding harness for a replay buffer of raw tool observations, dropping stale entries by age instead of rewriting them.
what.quote: we replace the running summary with a replay buffer of raw tool observations

result.text: 41% fewer tokens per task and 31% fewer retries across 40 long-horizon tasks, with no accuracy loss.
result.quote: 41% fewer tokens per task and 31% fewer retries across 40 long-horizon tasks

why.text: Long tasks fail on lost identifiers, not lost intent: a summary keeps the plan and throws away the exact strings the agent needs to act.

catch.text: Every task is a Python repository under 2,000 files, so the result says nothing about large TypeScript monorepos.
catch.quote: all 40 tasks are Python repositories under 2,000 files

summary.excerpt: We replace the running summary with a replay buffer of raw tool observations and drop entries older than the horizon. All 40 tasks are Python repositories under 2,000 files.

picks.title: Detecting Re-encoded Watermarks in Generated Images
picks.basis_label: vetted preprint via 63 Hugging Face upvotes

what.text: Tested whether image watermarks survive the ordinary abuse of a screenshot workflow: JPEG re-encoding, cropping and rescaling.
what.quote: we re-encode at quality 70 and crop to the central 60%

result.text: 94% detection after re-encoding and 81% after crop and rescale, against a 52% baseline.
result.quote: 94% after re-encoding, 81% after crop and rescale

why.text: Provenance claims are only useful if they survive the first thing a human does to an image.

catch.text: Two generators only, both diffusion-based, and no evaluation on synthetic video.
catch.quote: two diffusion generators; video is out of scope

summary.excerpt: We re-encode at quality 70 and crop to the central 60% before probing. Two diffusion generators; video is out of scope.

picks.title: Evaluating deep agents in production
picks.basis_label: lab post: the lab's own claim

what.text: Describes what changed when a coding agent went from a benchmark harness to a product with real traces.

result.text: No benchmark numbers, but a concrete list of what they now measure first: retries, truncations and abandoned steps.

why.text: Production traces are longer, messier and full of tool errors the benchmarks never include.
why.quote: half of the failures we see are tool errors, not reasoning errors

catch.text: A vendor write-up: no control group and no published traces.

summary.excerpt: Half of the failures we see are tool errors, not reasoning errors. Here is what we measure first in production.

picks.title: Gated Recurrent Transformers Stay Cheap Past 128k Tokens

summary.excerpt: We add a gated recurrent state to a transformer block and measure attention cost past 128k tokens.

picks.title: Durable execution for agent loops
picks.basis_label: lab post: the lab's own claim

what.text: Walks through wrapping an agent loop in durable execution so a crashed step resumes instead of restarting the whole task.

why.text: A 300-step task that restarts on failure burns the token budget twice.
why.quote: a retry that restarts the workflow pays for the whole trajectory again

catch.text: Useful engineering, but it is one vendor's opinion of the right boundary.

summary.excerpt: A retry that restarts the workflow pays for the whole trajectory again.

rising.title: Sparse Attention With a Learned Sketch
rising.basis_label: preprint from a recognised lab's authors, not yet independently vetted

what.text: Learns a sketch of the attention pattern and attends only to the tokens the sketch keeps.
what.quote: a learned sketch selects the keys the query actually needs

result.text: 1.8x throughput at 256k context with a 0.6 point drop on one long-context benchmark.

why.text: Long-context agents stop paying quadratic cost for context they rarely use.

catch.text: One benchmark and one model size, with no tool-use evaluation.

summary.excerpt: A learned sketch selects the keys the query actually needs.

rising.title: Agent Traces as a Training Signal
rising.basis_label: preprint from a recognised lab's authors, not yet independently vetted

summary.excerpt: We turn recorded agent traces into a preference signal for training the next policy.

rising.title: Benchmarking Browser Agents on Real Checkouts
rising.basis_label: preprint from a recognised lab's authors, not yet independently vetted

what.text: Ran browser agents against real storefronts rather than a static benchmark harness.
what.quote: we evaluate on live checkouts instead of a fixed harness

result.text: A 38% completion rate over 60 tasks, with half the failures coming from a changed layout.

why.text: A benchmark that never changes cannot measure the failure real sites cause.

catch.text: Three sites only, all in one jurisdiction.

summary.excerpt: We evaluate on live checkouts instead of a fixed harness.
